lines.text: Vocabulary
lines.spoken: Vocabulary.

lines.text: Cloud Basics
lines.spoken: Cloud Basics.

lines.text: NIST SP 800-145: "The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing." The standard set of definitions for cloud computing. It also compares cloud services and deployment strategies.
lines.spoken: NIST S.P. 800-145: "The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing." The standard set of definitions for cloud computing. It also compares cloud services and deployment strategies.

lines.text: Public cloud: open for public use.
lines.spoken: Public cloud: open for public use.

lines.text: Private cloud: used only by the client organization, either on-premises (on-prem) or in a dedicated area at a cloud provider.
lines.spoken: Private cloud: used only by the client organization, either on-premises (on-prem) or in a dedicated area at a cloud provider.

lines.text: Community cloud: shared between several organizations.
lines.spoken: Community cloud: shared between several organizations.

lines.text: Hybrid cloud: made of two or more clouds, which can include on-prem services.
lines.spoken: Hybrid cloud: made of two or more clouds, which can include on-prem services.

lines.text: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service): you rent infrastructure and buy virtual power to run your software as needed. Like running a virtual server on a virtual disk. Similar to a utility company model, because you pay for what you use.
lines.spoken: I.A.A.S. (Infrastructure as a Service): you rent infrastructure and buy virtual power to run your software as needed. Like running a virtual server on a virtual disk. Similar to a utility company model, because you pay for what you use.

lines.text: PaaS (Platform as a Service): provides everything except applications. Covers all phases of the system development life cycle (SDLC) and can use APIs, website portals, or gateway software. Tends to be proprietary, which causes problems if the customer moves away from the provider's platform.
lines.spoken: PAZ (Platform as a Service): provides everything except applications. Covers all phases of the system development life cycle (SDLC) and can use A.P.I.s, website portals, or gateway software. Tends to be proprietary, which causes problems if the customer moves away from the provider's platform.

lines.text: SaaS (Software as a Service): a complete packaged solution. The software is rented to the user, usually through a front end or web portal. The user can use it from anywhere, and the company pays a per-use fee.
lines.spoken: SASS (Software as a Service): a complete packaged solution. The software is rented to the user, usually through a front end or web portal. The user can use it from anywhere, and the company pays a per-use fee.

lines.text: CSP (cloud service provider): a provider such as Azure, AWS, or GCP (Google Cloud Platform).
lines.spoken: CSP (cloud service provider): a provider such as Azure, AWS, or GCP (Google Cloud Platform).

lines.text: Shared responsibility model: describes which security duties belong to the customer and which belong to the CSP. It depends on the service model. Amazon publishes one for AWS.
lines.spoken: Shared responsibility model: describes which security duties belong to the customer and which belong to the CSP. It depends on the service model. Amazon publishes one for AWS.

lines.text: SLA (service level agreement): the contracted level of guaranteed service between the cloud provider and the customer.
lines.spoken: SLA (service level agreement): the contracted level of guaranteed service between the cloud provider and the customer.

lines.text: DR/BCP (disaster recovery and business continuity plan): how the provider responds to fire, storms, natural disasters, or power loss, and what continued service it guarantees.
lines.spoken: D.R. and B.C.P. (disaster recovery and business continuity plan): how the provider responds to fire, storms, natural disasters, or power loss, and what continued service it guarantees.

lines.text: Development Methodologies
lines.spoken: Development Methodologies.

lines.text: Waterfall: development and project management method with at least five to seven phases in strict linear order. A phase can't start until the previous one is complete.
lines.spoken: Waterfall: development and project management method with at least five to seven phases in strict linear order. A phase can't start until the previous one is complete.

lines.text: Agile: development and project management process that breaks a project into stages, with constant collaboration with stakeholders and continuous improvement and iteration at every stage.
lines.spoken: Agile: development and project management process that breaks a project into stages, with constant collaboration with stakeholders and continuous improvement and iteration at every stage.

lines.text: Backlog: the committed list of work in Agile.
lines.spoken: Backlog: the committed list of work in Agile.

lines.text: User stories: what Agile teams turn an idea into, along with a feature specification.
lines.spoken: User stories: what Agile teams turn an idea into, along with a feature specification.

lines.text: Scrum: a framework related to Agile. Teams learn through experience, self-organize, and reflect on wins and losses to improve. It defines a set of meetings, tools, and roles.
lines.spoken: Scrum: a framework related to Agile. Teams learn through experience, self-organize, and reflect on wins and losses to improve. It defines a set of meetings, tools, and roles.

lines.text: Sprint: a short, time-boxed period in which a Scrum team completes a predefined amount of work. A key concept of Scrum and Agile.
lines.spoken: Sprint: a short, time-boxed period in which a Scrum team completes a predefined amount of work. A key concept of Scrum and Agile.

lines.text: Lean: management philosophy that eliminates waste of time and resources across the business. Agile is an implementation of Lean.
lines.spoken: Lean: management philosophy that eliminates waste of time and resources across the business. Agile is an implementation of Lean.

lines.text: Kanban: scheduling system for lean development and just-in-time (JIT) manufacturing, developed by Taiichi Ohno of Toyota. Agile uses it.
lines.spoken: Kanban: scheduling system for lean development and just-in-time (JIT) manufacturing, developed by Taiichi Ohno of Toyota. Agile uses it.

lines.text: Extreme Programming (EP): development method that improves quality and adapts to the changing needs of the customer, with iterative, frequent small releases. More commonly called XP; that abbreviation is not in the book.
lines.spoken: Extreme Programming (EP): development method that improves quality and adapts to the changing needs of the customer, with iterative, frequent small releases. More commonly called XP; that abbreviation is not in the book.

lines.text: SDLC: stands for system development life cycle, and is also often used for secure development life cycle.
lines.spoken: SDLC: stands for system development life cycle, and is also often used for secure development life cycle.

lines.text: DevOps: the convergence of many technical, project management, and management movements, built on Lean, Theory of Constraints, resilience engineering, learning organizations, safety culture, human factors, and more.
lines.spoken: DevOps: the convergence of many technical, project management, and management movements, built on Lean, Theory of Constraints, resilience engineering, learning organizations, safety culture, human factors, and more.

lines.text: CI/CD and Serverless
lines.spoken: C.I. C.D. and Serverless.

lines.text: CI (Continuous Integration): programmers merge code changes into a central repository multiple times a day.
lines.spoken: CI (Continuous Integration): programmers merge code changes into a central repository multiple times a day.

lines.text: CD (Continuous Delivery): sits on top of CI and automates the entire software release process.
lines.spoken: CD (Continuous Delivery): sits on top of CI and automates the entire software release process.

lines.text: CI/CD pipeline: each code change triggers an automated build-and-test sequence that gives feedback to the programmer. The goal is full automation, with each run logged and visible to the whole team.
lines.spoken: C.I. C.D. pipeline: each code change triggers an automated build-and-test sequence that gives feedback to the programmer. The goal is full automation, with each run logged and visible to the whole team.

lines.text: Smoke tests: quick sanity checks from the user's point of view, run first in a multistage test phase.
lines.spoken: Smoke tests: quick sanity checks from the user's point of view, run first in a multistage test phase.

lines.text: Staging (beta) environment: deployment environment used internally by the product team before production.
lines.spoken: Staging (beta) environment: deployment environment used internally by the product team before production.

lines.text: Serverless computing (FaaS, function as a service): developers build and run applications without managing the server infrastructure. The cloud provider handles servers, virtual machines, networking, and scaling. Servers still exist; developers are just abstracted away from them.
lines.spoken: Serverless computing (FaaS, function as a service): developers build and run applications without managing the server infrastructure. The cloud provider handles servers, virtual machines, networking, and scaling. Servers still exist; developers are just abstracted away from them.

lines.text: Function: a small, self-contained piece of code that performs a specific task. Usually event-driven.
lines.spoken: Function: a small, self-contained piece of code that performs a specific task. Usually event-driven.

lines.text: AWS Lambda: one of the most popular serverless architectures. You run code without provisioning servers and pay only for the compute time you use. The book's figure captions spell it "Lamda."
lines.spoken: AWS Lambda: one of the most popular serverless architectures. You run code without provisioning servers and pay only for the compute time you use. The book's figure captions spell it "Lamda."

lines.text: Containers and Orchestration
lines.spoken: Containers and Orchestration.

lines.text: Container image: bundles a program and its dependencies into a single artifact under a root file system.
lines.spoken: Container image: bundles a program and its dependencies into a single artifact under a root file system.

lines.text: Container image layer: each layer adds, removes, or modifies files from the layer before it. Each parent reference is a pointer.
lines.spoken: Container image layer: each layer adds, removes, or modifies files from the layer before it. Each parent reference is a pointer.

lines.text: Docker: one of the most popular container runtime engines. Packages an executable and pushes it to a remote registry for others to pull.
lines.spoken: Docker: one of the most popular container runtime engines. Packages an executable and pushes it to a remote registry for others to pull.

lines.text: Container registry: stores images. Offered by AWS, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure, or run privately with open-source or commercial systems.
lines.spoken: Container registry: stores images. Offered by AWS, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure, or run privately with open-source or commercial systems.

lines.text: Docker Hub: Docker's public image repository.
lines.spoken: Docker Hub: Docker's public image repository.

lines.text: Dockerfile: a file that automates the creation of a Docker container image.
lines.spoken: Dockerfile: a file that automates the creation of a Docker container image.

lines.text: OCI (Open Container Initiative) image format: the standardized form of the Docker image format, the most popular image format.
lines.spoken: OCI (Open Container Initiative) image format: the standardized form of the Docker image format, the most popular image format.

lines.text: Container orchestration: managing, deploying, and orchestrating containers.
lines.spoken: Container orchestration: managing, deploying, and orchestrating containers.

lines.text: Kubernetes (k8s): one of the most popular container orchestration frameworks, originally developed by Google. Automates the distribution, scheduling, and orchestration of containers across a cluster.
lines.spoken: Kubernetes (k8s): one of the most popular container orchestration frameworks, originally developed by Google. Automates the distribution, scheduling, and orchestration of containers across a cluster.

lines.text: Nomad: container management and orchestration platform. The book says "HashCorp"; the company is HashiCorp.
lines.spoken: Nomad: container management and orchestration platform. The book says "HashCorp"; the company is HashiCorp.

lines.text: Apache Mesos: a distributed Linux kernel with native support for launching containers with Docker and AppC images.
lines.spoken: Apache Mesos: a distributed Linux kernel with native support for launching containers with Docker and AppC images.

lines.text: Docker Swarm: container cluster management and orchestration integrated with the Docker Engine.
lines.spoken: Docker Swarm: container cluster management and orchestration integrated with the Docker Engine.

lines.text: Master: Kubernetes component that coordinates all cluster activity: scheduling, scaling, and deploying applications.
lines.spoken: Master: Kubernetes component that coordinates all cluster activity: scheduling, scaling, and deploying applications.

lines.text: Node: a VM or physical server that acts as a worker machine in a Kubernetes cluster.
lines.spoken: Node: a VM or physical server that acts as a worker machine in a Kubernetes cluster.

lines.text: Pod: a group of one or more containers with shared storage and networking, plus a specification for how to run them. Each pod has an IP address and should be able to reach all other pods.
lines.spoken: Pod: a group of one or more containers with shared storage and networking, plus a specification for how to run them. Each pod has an IP address and should be able to reach all other pods.

lines.text: kubectl: the official Kubernetes client. The book misspells it "kubctl" once.
lines.spoken: kubectl: the official Kubernetes client. The book misspells it "kubctl" once.

lines.text: kubeadm: Kubernetes component that bootstraps a minimum viable cluster and manages nodes in a multi-node cluster.
lines.spoken: kubeadm: Kubernetes component that bootstraps a minimum viable cluster and manages nodes in a multi-node cluster.

lines.text: minikube: a lightweight Kubernetes implementation for learning.
lines.spoken: minikube: a lightweight Kubernetes implementation for learning.

lines.text: GKE (Google Kubernetes Engine): GCP's hosted Kubernetes as a Service. Azure and AWS offer similar services.
lines.spoken: GKE (Google Kubernetes Engine): GCP's hosted Kubernetes as a Service. Azure and AWS offer similar services.

lines.text: Micro-segmentation: network segmentation at the VM level or between containers, regardless of VLAN or subnet. Must be application aware.
lines.spoken: Micro-segmentation: network segmentation at the VM level or between containers, regardless of V-lan or subnet. Must be application aware.

lines.text: Contiv: open-source project for micro-segmentation policy-based services in container environments. Covered in Chapter 3.
lines.spoken: Contiv: open-source project for micro-segmentation policy-based services in container environments. Covered in Chapter 3.

lines.text: DevSecOps and Software Testing
lines.spoken: DevSecOps and Software Testing.

lines.text: DevSecOps: moving security to the start of the development life cycle and building security practices into the CI/CD pipeline.
lines.spoken: DevSecOps: moving security to the start of the development life cycle and building security practices into the C.I. C.D. pipeline.

lines.text: Shifting security to the left: moving security earlier into design, coding, and testing.
lines.spoken: Shifting security to the left: moving security earlier into design, coding, and testing.

lines.text: Secure by default: make it easy for developers to write secure code and hard to make dangerous mistakes, with secure defaults in templates and frameworks.
lines.spoken: Secure by default: make it easy for developers to write secure code and hard to make dangerous mistakes, with secure defaults in templates and frameworks.

lines.text: OWASP Proactive Controls: OWASP's collection of secure development practices every developer should follow.
lines.spoken: oh-wasp Proactive Controls: oh-wasp's collection of secure development practices every developer should follow.

lines.text: SAST (static application security testing): a software assurance method.
lines.spoken: sast (static application security testing): a software assurance method.

lines.text: DAST (dynamic application security testing): a software assurance method.
lines.spoken: dast (dynamic application security testing): a software assurance method.

lines.text: Fuzzing (fuzz testing): sends random data to the unit being tested to find input validation issues, program failures, buffer overflows, and other flaws. Works on applications, operating systems, infrastructure devices, IoT devices, and more.
lines.spoken: Fuzzing (fuzz testing): sends random data to the unit being tested to find input validation issues, program failures, buffer overflows, and other flaws. Works on applications, operating systems, infrastructure devices, I.O.T. devices, and more.

lines.text: Fuzzer: a tool that performs fuzzing.
lines.spoken: Fuzzer: a tool that performs fuzzing.

lines.text: Cisco Umbrella
lines.spoken: Cisco Umbrella.

lines.text: Cisco Umbrella: cloud-delivered solution that blocks malicious destinations using DNS. Evolved from the OpenDNS acquisition.
lines.spoken: Cisco Umbrella: cloud-delivered solution that blocks malicious destinations using DNS. Evolved from the Open D.N.S. acquisition.

lines.text: OpenDNS: a suite of consumer products for a faster, safer, more reliable Internet.
lines.spoken: Open D.N.S.: a suite of consumer products for a faster, safer, more reliable Internet.

lines.text: Anycast: all Umbrella data centers announce the same IP address, and requests go to the fastest, lowest-latency data center. Gives the recursive DNS service reliability and scale.
lines.spoken: Anycast: all Umbrella data centers announce the same IP address, and requests go to the fastest, lowest-latency data center. Gives the recursive DNS service reliability and scale.

lines.text: Fast flux: DNS technique botnets use to hide phishing and malware sites behind an ever-changing network of compromised hosts acting as proxies.
lines.spoken: Fast flux: DNS technique botnets use to hide phishing and malware sites behind an ever-changing network of compromised hosts acting as proxies.

lines.text: SIG (secure Internet gateway): Umbrella's cloud-based proxy, which inspects only requests for risky domains.
lines.spoken: SIG (secure Internet gateway): Umbrella's cloud-based proxy, which inspects only requests for risky domains.

lines.text: Risky domain: a domain that hosts both malicious and safe content, usually because users can upload and share content. Examples: facebook.com, reddit.com, pastebin.com.
lines.spoken: Risky domain: a domain that hosts both malicious and safe content, usually because users can upload and share content. Examples: facebook dot com, reddit dot com, pastebin dot com.

lines.text: Cisco Umbrella Investigate: gives access to Umbrella's global intelligence to enrich security data and events and help with incident response. Through a web console or an API.
lines.spoken: Cisco Umbrella Investigate: gives access to Umbrella's global intelligence to enrich security data and events and help with incident response. Through a web console or an API.

lines.text: Email Security
lines.spoken: Email Security.

lines.text: Cisco Secure Email Threat Defense: Cisco's cloud-based email security solution. Protects against ransomware, business email compromise (BEC), phishing, spear phishing, whaling, and other email attacks. The book uses this name for what its own figures and review questions call Cisco Cloud Email Security (CES). Not in the book: Cisco now sells Secure Email Threat Defense as a separate API-based Microsoft 365 product, and the gateway formerly called CES is Secure Email Cloud Gateway.
lines.spoken: Cisco Secure Email Threat Defense: Cisco's cloud-based email security solution. Protects against ransomware, business email compromise (BEC), phishing, spear phishing, whaling, and other email attacks. The book uses this name for what its own figures and review questions call Cisco Cloud Email Security (CES). Not in the book: Cisco now sells Secure Email Threat Defense as a separate API-based Microsoft 365 product, and the gateway formerly called CES is Secure Email Cloud Gateway.

lines.text: AsyncOS: the operating system of Cisco Secure Email, Cisco Secure Web Appliance, and the cloud email security solution.
lines.spoken: async O.S.: the operating system of Cisco Secure Email, Cisco Secure Web Appliance, and the cloud email security solution.

lines.text: CASE (Cisco Context Adaptive Scanning Engine): antispam engine.
lines.spoken: case (Cisco Context Adaptive Scanning Engine): antispam engine.

lines.text: FED (Forged Email Detection): detects spear phishing by checking parts of the SMTP message for manipulation, including the "Envelope-From," "Reply To," and "From" headers.
lines.spoken: FED (Forged Email Detection): detects spear phishing by checking parts of the SMTP message for manipulation, including the "Envelope-From," "Reply To," and "From" headers.

lines.text: SPF (Sender Policy Framework): used for sender authentication.
lines.spoken: SPF (Sender Policy Framework): used for sender authentication.

lines.text: DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail): used for domain authentication.
lines.spoken: D-kim (DomainKeys Identified Mail): used for domain authentication.

lines.text: DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance): used for domain authentication.
lines.spoken: D-mark (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance): used for domain authentication.

lines.text: S/MIME (Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions): standards-based method to send and receive secure, verified email. Uses a public and private key pair to encrypt or sign messages.
lines.spoken: S mime (Secure or Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions): standards-based method to send and receive secure, verified email. Uses a public and private key pair to encrypt or sign messages.

lines.text: Cisco Cloud Security Products
lines.spoken: Cisco Cloud Security Products.

lines.text: Attack Surface Management: industry term for proactively identifying and managing an organization's vulnerabilities and attack vectors in its digital ecosystem.
lines.spoken: Attack Surface Management: industry term for proactively identifying and managing an organization's vulnerabilities and attack vectors in its digital ecosystem.

lines.text: Cisco Attack Surface Management (formerly Cisco Secure Cloud Insights): cloud-native platform that bridges gaps between separate security tools and gives visibility into risk across the whole cyber asset ecosystem.
lines.spoken: Cisco Attack Surface Management (formerly Cisco Secure Cloud Insights): cloud-native platform that bridges gaps between separate security tools and gives visibility into risk across the whole cyber asset ecosystem.

lines.text: Cisco Secure Analytics (formerly Stealthwatch): on-prem analytics that uses NetFlow and context from the Cisco network. Covered in Chapter 5.
lines.spoken: Cisco Secure Analytics (formerly Stealthwatch): on-prem analytics that uses NetFlow and context from the Cisco network. Covered in Chapter 5.

lines.text: Cisco Secure Cloud Analytics: SaaS that identifies internal and external threats across on-prem, public cloud, and hybrid cloud environments.
lines.spoken: Cisco Secure Cloud Analytics: SASS that identifies internal and external threats across on-prem, public cloud, and hybrid cloud environments.

lines.text: Cisco Secure Cloud Sensor: virtual or physical appliance needed for Secure Cloud Analytics to monitor on-prem networks.
lines.spoken: Cisco Secure Cloud Sensor: virtual or physical appliance needed for Secure Cloud Analytics to monitor on-prem networks.

lines.text: North/south traffic: traffic across the perimeter.
lines.spoken: North or south traffic: traffic across the perimeter.

lines.text: East/west traffic: lateral movement inside the network.
lines.spoken: East or west traffic: lateral movement inside the network.

lines.text: AppDynamics (AppD): Cisco-acquired company. Gives end-to-end application visibility and performance insight, and builds a dynamic topology map of all applications.
lines.spoken: AppDynamics (AppD): Cisco-acquired company. Gives end-to-end application visibility and performance insight, and builds a dynamic topology map of all applications.

lines.text: Workload Optimization Manager: Cisco agentless server application on a VM. Maps relationships between applications and infrastructure, anticipates performance and efficiency risks, and recommends actions.
lines.spoken: Workload Optimization Manager: Cisco agentless server application on a VM. Maps relationships between applications and infrastructure, anticipates performance and efficiency risks, and recommends actions.

lines.text: Cisco Secure Workload (formerly Tetration): uses rich traffic flow telemetry for data center use cases, with advanced analytics. Supports on-prem and public cloud workloads.
lines.spoken: Cisco Secure Workload (formerly Tetration): uses rich traffic flow telemetry for data center use cases, with advanced analytics. Supports on-prem and public cloud workloads.

lines.text: Secure Connector: makes an outgoing connection from the orchestrator's network to the Secure Workload cluster, used as a reverse tunnel to reach the orchestrator API server.
lines.spoken: Secure Connector: makes an outgoing connection from the orchestrator's network to the Secure Workload cluster, used as a reverse tunnel to reach the orchestrator API server.

lines.text: ADM (Application Dependency Mapping): Secure Workload function that gives insight into complex applications in a data center or in the cloud.
lines.spoken: ADM (Application Dependency Mapping): Secure Workload function that gives insight into complex applications in a data center or in the cloud.

lines.text: Connectors: Secure Workload integrations for flow ingestion, inventory enrichment, and alert notifications.
lines.spoken: Connectors: Secure Workload integrations for flow ingestion, inventory enrichment, and alert notifications.

lines.text: Flow Observation: per-minute aggregation of each unique flow in Secure Workload.
lines.spoken: Flow Observation: per-minute aggregation of each unique flow in Secure Workload.

lines.text: Consumer and Provider: the two sides of a flow. The Consumer starts the flow and the Provider responds, like client and server.
lines.spoken: Consumer and Provider: the two sides of a flow. The Consumer starts the flow and the Provider responds, like client and server.

lines.text: XDR (eXtended Detection and Response): aggregates telemetry from many security tools into central storage, analyzes the normalized data to detect malicious activity, and speeds response and remediation.
lines.spoken: XDR (eXtended Detection and Response): aggregates telemetry from many security tools into central storage, analyzes the normalized data to detect malicious activity, and speeds response and remediation.

lines.text: SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) and SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response): earlier attempts to integrate disconnected security tools and reduce alerts. The book says they fall short.

lines.text: Cisco Talos: Cisco's threat intelligence organization, used by Umbrella, email security, and XDR.
lines.spoken: Cisco Talos: Cisco's threat intelligence organization, used by Umbrella, email security, and XDR.
